description: Audit UI / marketing copy objectively: readability (Flesch reading ease + grade level), average sentence length, passive voice, jargon/hype words, filler, user-focus ('you' vs 'we'), and weak CTAs. Returns metrics plus specific flagged phrases and fixes. The machine-checkable slice of UX writing — pair with get_design_doc('ux-writing') for voice/tone judgment. It reads source and does not measure anything: no usability session is run, no A/B result is read, and no finding here is or can be a statement about whether the copy actually works for a reader. It also has no notion of register: it has no way to tell short UI copy from long-form prose, so a paragraph of accurate technical documentation can draw more jargon/filler hits than a paragraph of real hype. Returns markdown plus structured output: findings (rule, severity, message, fix, doc, line), a severity summary, a machine-readable `notVisible` list of what it could not check, and a `metrics` block carrying the same words/sentences/avgSentenceLen/Flesch/grade-level/you-we numbers the markdown table prints.

text.description: The copy to audit (a headline, paragraph, button label, error message, or full page copy)

name: audit_ux_copy

findings.description: Every finding, in the order the markdown report lists them.

doc.description: Knowledge-base id backing the claim — read it with get_design_doc.

file.description: Path relative to the audited directory, when a directory was audited.

message.description: The fact about the source that made the rule fire.

severity.description: How the rule grades this finding.

metrics.description: The metrics table the markdown half prints, as numbers. Facts about the text's shape, not measurements of how it reads — see `notVisible`.

avgSentenceLen.description: words / sentences, to one decimal. The target the report grades is ≤ 20.

fleschReadingEase.description: Flesch reading ease, rounded. Higher is easier; the target the report grades is ≥ 60. Computed from the two counts above and a heuristic syllable count, all three of which `notVisible` bounds.

gradeLevel.description: Flesch–Kincaid grade level, floored at 0. The report grades it against ≤ 8 but raises no finding on it — this field is the only structured form of that row.

sentences.description: Runs split on `.`/`!`/`?` followed by whitespace, with no abbreviation handling, OR on a bare newline with no punctuation at all — a two-line toast or tooltip counts as two sentences. Never 0.

weCount.description: Occurrences of we/our/us/we're. A finding fires when this exceeds `youCount`.

words.description: Tokens matched by /[a-z0-9']+/ — ASCII only, and never 0: an empty match set is reported as 1. See `notVisible`.

notVisible.description: What this audit structurally could not check, one limitation per entry. Read it as a peer of `findings`: silence on a subject named here is this tool's reach, not a clean result. Nothing any of these tools reports is measured.

summary.description: Counts by severity. Always agrees with `findings` — it is derived from the same list.

title: Audit Ux Copy
